title: The Complete Guide to Car Seat Installation
summary: Nearly half of all car seats are installed incorrectly. A CPST breaks down LATCH vs. seat belt installation, the top tether, and the one-inch test—everything you need to install your car seat right, every time.
body_markdown:
Installation is one of the most important things you will do with your child car seat. In fact, nearly half of all child car seats are[installed incorrectly](https://www.nhtsa.gov/press-releases/national-car-seat-check-saturday-2024) according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), which is a staggering amount when you consider that they exist to keep children safe. However, it does not have to be a stressful experience for your family. If you ensure you follow the important steps outlined below, you and your family will be able to install your car seat correctly, every time!


It’s not at all unusual for those new to parenting and childcare to find themselves bereft in the back of their car, fumbling with car seat fittings and scratching their heads—and the same often can be the case for seasoned parents who’ve simply bought a new one.


That’s where Child Passenger Safety Technicians (CPSTs) come in. We spend our days immersed in car seats, so we can break down exactly what’s involved in correct installation and fitment.


This guide covers the essentials of how to install a car seat: choosing a method, installing with LATCH, installing with the seat belt, the top tether, and confirming the install is tight. There’s also more information in our video, Car Seats: How to with the Gurus, and in our accompanying article Car Seat Safety: Mistakes, Expiration Dates, and Care.


- **What Are the Two Ways to Install a Car Seat?**
- **How Do I Install a Car Seat Using LATCH?**
- **How Do I Install a Car Seat Using the Seat Belt?**
- **Do I Need to Use the Top Tether?**
- **How Do I Know My Car Seat Is Installed Correctly?**
- **Where Can I Get My Car Seat Installation Checked by a Professional?**
- **Frequently Asked Questions**
- **Bottom Line**


Question Short answer


**Is LATCH or a seat belt installation safer?** Neither—NHTSA considers both equally safe when installed correctly


**What's the LATCH weight limit?** 65 lbs combined child + car seat weight for the lower anchors (check your seat's label—some set it lower)


**Do I need the top tether?** Yes, on every forward-facing install, regardless of whether the base uses LATCH or the seat belt


**How do I know the install is tight enough?** The inch test: less than 1 inch of movement side-to-side or front-to-back at the belt path


## What Are the Two Ways to Install a Car Seat?


There are two ways to install car seats: LATCH and seat belt. Both are equally safe as long as they’re done correctly, but you need to choose one or the other. They should never be combined.


LATCH stands for Lower Anchors and Tethers for Children and refers to built-in vehicle anchor points that let you install a car seat without the seat belt. There is a federal standard that limits LATCH connections to 65 pounds including both the seat and the child, so they’re typically found on infant seats designed for newborn babies to children up to 18 months old. Typically, they are easiest to use in outboard seats where the anchor points are easily accessible.


Seat belt installations involve threading the belt through a designated path in the child seat. Both the lap and the shoulder belts should thread through the base of the car seat and click into the seat belt anchor—just as they do when adults connect a seat belt. Unlike the LATCH method, there is no weight limit with seat belt installations, so they become the only option when children have outgrown infant seats with LATCH fittings, and they work equally well in outboard or center-seat positions.


LATCH Seat belt


**Safety** Equally safe when installed correctly Equally safe when installed correctly


**Weight limit** 65 lbs combined child + seat (lower anchors only—check your seat's label) No combined weight limit; becomes the only option once LATCH is outgrown


**Best for** Outboard seating positions with accessible anchors Center seating positions, or once the LATCH weight limit is reached


**Rule** Never combine with the seat belt at the same seating position Never combine with LATCH at the same seating position


## How Do I Install a Car Seat Using LATCH?


LATCH systems are really simple to install, and it’s always best to start by locating the lower anchors in the vehicle’s seat. These are not the anchor points for conventional seat belts—they’re the metal bars in the crease of the vehicle seat. Your vehicle’s Owner’s Manual can help locate the LATCH anchor points.


Infant car seats—the type usually fitted with LATCH attachments—typically have a detachable base, which makes for two big perks. The first is that it’s easy to move a sleeping child—you just unclip the seat shell from the base and carry it or place it in a compatible stroller—and the second is that you don’t have to navigate installation every time you use the seat; you simply install the base once, then click in the infant seat the top of it every time you ride with baby.


Make sure the base is at the proper recline angle by lifting the recline foot adjuster. You can do this by looking at the bubble in the spirit level in the car seat’s base, which falls between the lines when the recline angle is correct. When it’s level, pull the base straps tight to secure it in place, and don’t forget to push down on the base while you’re tightening the straps to remove slack, because this is where most loose install errors occur.


We walk through everything described above in our video Car Seats: All you need to know with CarGurus and **[Chicco](https://www.chiccousa.com/)** , so you can see what it looks like in practice.


## How Do I Install a Car Seat Using the Seat Belt?


As with the LATCH method, the first step is to adjust the recline angle of the car seat or base to ensure it is level. Then pull the seat belt all the way out, thread it up through the belt path on one side, over the middle, and down through the path on the opposite side. Buckle the seat belt.


Push firmly down on the base with your body weight. While holding it down, pull up on the shoulder belt to remove all slack, and lock the belt in place using the built-in lock-off on the base.


Please note that each car seat has its own versions of belt paths and lock-offs, so always check specific steps in your car seat’s manual. Many new car seats have patented lock-off designs that make installation a breeze, so don’t be intimidated!


Check your vehicle’s manual if you’re unsure about what type of seat belt it has.


## Do I Need to Use the Top Tether?


The car seat top tether is an adjustable strap with a metal hook that connects the top of a forward-facing car seat to the vehicle’s anchor point. The anchor point often has a boat anchor icon to designate its location, and is usually found on the back of the seat, on the rear shelf, on the ceiling, or on the floor; check the vehicle’s manual if it’s not obvious, and to make sure that you are not mistaking a cargo anchor point for the top tether anchor.


Top tethers should always be used with forward-facing car seats, because they significantly reduce a child’s forward head movement in a crash. People often forget about them, and they’re one of the most common ways in which car seats are fitted incorrectly.


Top tethers do not typically feature on rear-facing car seats, and most manufacturers recommend against using them when convertible car seats are in rear-facing mode –as usual, check your seat’s manual first. In short, as a rule of thumb, if a car seat is facing forward, you should use the top tether.


## How Do I Know My Car Seat Is Installed Correctly?


The car seat inch test is an easy way to check whether you’ve installed a car seat correctly. After you’ve fitted the seat—either with a latch or a seat belt—grab both sides of the seat at the belt paths and try to shift it from side to side and front to back.


If the seat moves by more than one inch in any direction, it isn’t secure enough and you need to reinstall it. If there is no more than an inch of movement in any direction, then you’ve properly secured the car seat and you’re good to go.


## Where Can I Get My Car Seat Installation Checked by a Professional?


Car seat manufacturers typically provide resources, like QR codes, video tutorials and colored touchpoints, to guide parents and help them feel confident in their installation ability. However, if you want a professional to examine your car seat installation and offer advice, check out the[NHTSA’s car seat inspection locator](https://www.nhtsa.gov/vehicle-safety/car-seats-and-booster-seats#installation-help-inspection) . Enter your city and state or zip code, and you’ll find a directory of certified technicians who will check your car seat installation. Some locations offer virtual inspections too.


[Safe Kids Worldwide](https://events.safekids.org/) offers a similar car seat checking service, and conducts regular events and workshops aimed at promoting child safety. The NHTSA is a government body and Safe Kids Worldwide is a nonprofit organization, so car seat checks administered by them are often free of charge and typically take about 20-30 minutes.


Some manufacturers and retailers allow parents and caregivers to try before you buy. If you’re not sure whether a particular model will fit in your car, contract or visit your local store and ask about test installation before you commit to a purchase. This is particularly worthwhile if your car’s interior is on the tight side or if it has an unusual back seat.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is LATCH safer than a seat belt installation?


No. As long as they’re installed correctly, both LATCH and seat belt installations are equally safe, according to[NHTSA](https://www.nhtsa.gov/vehicle-safety/car-seats-and-booster-seats) .


### What is the LATCH weight limit?


The weight limit for LATCH car seats is generally a combined 65 lbs including both the seat and the child.


### Can I use LATCH and the seat belt together?


This one’s a hard no. Pick either LATCH or the seat belt, and never use the two together.


### Do I need to use the top tether if I'm installing with a seat belt?


Yes, but typically only with a forward-facing seat, and it doesn’t matter if the car seat is secured with a seat belt or with LATCH. Always check the manufacturer’s recommendations, but you don’t generally need to use the top tether with a rear-facing car seat.


### How often should I check my car seat installation?


As frequently as possible, but especially when you move the seat from car to car or transition to a different configuration (e.g. going from rear-facing to front). Remember to use the resources available to you and don’t forget the inch test!


## The Bottom Line


There aren’t many clear, right answers in parenting, but proper car seat installation is one of them. As bamboozling as they may seem to the uninitiated, good car seats are designed to be simple and easily installed, and don’t forget to use online resources to help verify proper use. Check NHTSA, Safe Kids Worldwide and car seat manufacturers if you want a little reassurance from an expert.


For those who want an even fuller picture, there’s even more information our articles, **[How to Choose the Right Car Seat](https://www.cargurus.com/research/articles/how-to-choose-the-right-car-seat)** and **[Car Seat Safety: Mistakes, Expiration Dates, and Care](https://www.cargurus.com/research/articles/car-seat-safety-mistakes-expiration-dates-and-care)** .
